title: I figured out how to get actually usable 3D models + animations out of GPT-6 Astra
author: Fearless_Brilliant51
selftext:
The entire character was modeled and animated from scratch in Blender.

This was the initial output from Astra after I gave it a reference image and asked it to create a 3D model for my character. From there, it was mostly a process of refining.  


https://preview.redd.it/mrgl2ouvndoh1.jpg?width=1000&format=pjpg&auto=webp&s=c4b69ee9e9cb5afe6c49878d0b9de91b117bae9e

I discovered that Astra works much better when you give it very targeted prompts with as few distractions as possible.

Instead of giving broad feedback like “the face looks wrong,” I would take a screenshot of the exact area that needed fixing, give it the same-angle image from the original reference, and point out exactly what was different. When I did that, it would often fix the issue correctly in one go. Even if you are unable to describe the issue accurately you can point to the area and Astra will figure it out, as long as the images are focused on the area itself and not the full character.

The main workflow I ended up using was to first generate reference images of the character from multiple perspectives: front, side, and an angled view. From there, I would send focused prompts targeting one specific component at a time.

I was also basically spamming prompts through steering while it worked. I didn’t have to wait for every task to finish before giving it the next instruction. I could keep spamming things while it worked and it would work through them until all were fixed.

I generated the original character references and texture references using ChatGPT on High before giving them to Astra.

For animation, the biggest thing was getting proper keyframe references. You can ask GPT to generate a single reference image showing your character across all the important key poses of an animation, then give that to Astra to recreate in Blender.

That worked surprisingly well. The main problem I ran into was mesh clipping during the animation.

Unfortunately, I ran out of weekly usage before I could finish refining the run animation, so this is where I had to leave it for now.

Overall, the biggest thing I learned is that Astra gets significantly better when you stop giving it broad instructions and start isolating problems visually. Good references, matching camera angles, and focused prompts made a massive difference.

I’m currently porting the rest of the game over to Unity as well.

Follow me on Twitter if you want to see more updates on the game:

[https://x.com/code3ater](https://x.com/code3ater)
